title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A subscriber that could not compile
summary: The quick fix that adds an event subscriber skipped the import line whenever the event type merely lived under the same package prefix.

highlights.title: A subpackage still needs an import
highlights.description: The fix asked whether the type name starts with the package of the open file. A screen in one package was told it could see an event two packages deeper. On a real project that answer is wrong 467 times.

highlights.title: Two packages that merely start alike
highlights.description: With no separator in the test, a file in one package passed for anything under a longer package name beginning with it.

highlights.title: An import that was only a lookalike
highlights.description: A longer import beginning the same way counted as the real one, and so did those words inside a comment. It has to be an import line now.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Adding a subscriber for an event declared in a subpackage now writes the import it needs.
Two packages that merely share a prefix are no longer treated as one.
A longer import, or the same words in a comment, no longer passes for the import of the event type.
An aliased import counts as importing the type.
